episodes.180072: A cold front triggered showers and thunderstorms. Some thunderstorms trained over the same areas, resulting in isolated instances of flooding and flash flooding around Baltimore.
episodes.180074: A severe thunderstorm tracked across Morrill County the afternoon of 27 June. The storm dropped large hail as it tracked into western Nebraska.
episodes.180104: Several clusters of thunderstorms produced widely scattered wind damage ahead of a slow-moving cold front.
episodes.180107: A couple bands of showers and thunderstorms produced localized wind damage and hail ahead of a weakening cold front.
episodes.180108: A couple bands of showers and thunderstorms produced localized wind damage and hail ahead of a weakening cold front.
episodes.180112: Clusters of thunderstorms produced gale-force wind gusts over area waterways ahead of a slow-moving cold front.
episodes.180113: Multiple bands of thunderstorms produced gale to near storm-force wind gusts over area waterways during the mid to late afternoon and early evening hours.
episodes.180204: A deep upper low over the Great Lakes and Ohio Valley moved toward the east coast along with a strong frontal boundary. A strong upper NW-SE oriented jet streak provided upper level divergence over the area, while 850mb flow increased out of the SW. Storms initiated along the pre-frontal surface trough and moved quickly eastward. Deep layer shear was strong and while there was a cap for the majority of the afternoon and early evening, it quickly broke as the pre frontal trough approached.
episodes.180224: Very dry surface conditions combined with an influx of mid-level moisture allowed for scattered virga showers and dry thunderstorms to develop over central and eastern NM during the afternoon hours of June 27th. Several of these produced severe downburst winds that impacted sporadic locations across eastern NM. These included Fort Sumner, Tucumcari, Estancia, Las Vegas, Carrizozo,  and Raton. Thankfully, there were no reports of damages or injuries.
episodes.180228: A large cluster of severe thunderstorms across central NC sagged southward, joined by new convection developing across central SC late in the evening on 6/26. Convection moved offshore between 3-4 AM on 6/27.
episodes.180229: A large cluster of severe thunderstorms across central NC sagged southward, joined by new convection developing across central SC late in the evening on 6/26. Convection moved offshore between 3-4 AM on 6/27.
episodes.180362: A low pressure system kicked off scattered thunderstorms across Northeastern Pennsylvania. The environment was unstable to support some severe thunderstorms in Luzerne County. These storms had strong winds that knocked down trees, with one landing on a house.
episodes.180364: A low pressure system brought showers and thunderstorms to Central New York. Daytime heating helped provide instability for strong to severe thunderstorms. Multiple severe storms developed across the region. Strong wind gusts and large hail caused some minor damage.
episodes.180408: Thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain in northern Delaware from the late afternoon into the nighttime hours of June 26.  Rainfall totals were as high as 2 to 5 inches.
episodes.180409: Thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain in northern New Jersey from the late afternoon into the nighttime hours of June 26.  Rainfall totals were as high as 2 to 5 inches.
episodes.180410: Thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain in eastern Pennsylvania from the late afternoon into the nighttime hours of June 26.  Rainfall totals were as high as 2 to 5 inches.
episodes.180411: Thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain in southeastern Pennsylvania during the late afternoon and evening of June 27.  Rainfall totals were as high as 1 to 2 inches.
episodes.180425: A long-lived supercell thunderstorm developed over the higher terrain of the central Laramie Range in far northwestern Laramie County near the Platte County late in the afternoon on 6/26. This thunderstorm quickly became severe as it tracked to the east-southeast across northern and eastern Laramie County through the early to mid evening hours, before exiting into western Nebraska. Multiple tornadoes were reported over rural eastern Laramie County, with an official NWS damage survey confirming two EF-1 tornadoes to the west and southwest of Albin, and an EF-0 tornado 8 miles ESE of Albin. In addition to the tornadoes, this storm also produced up to baseball sized hail near Gun Barrel. Additional isolated severe storms occurred over Converse County later in the evening.
episodes.180428: A long-lived supercell thunderstorm tracked across Kimball and Cheyenne Counties during the evening hours on 6/26, producing multiple tornadoes and numerous instances of golf ball to baseball sized hail. Most notably, a 3.5 inch diameter hailstone was observed in the town of Bushnell. An official NWS damage survey confirmed an EF-1 tornado to the southwest of Kimball between 8:01 and 8:05 PM MDT. Additional severe thunderstorms occurred over Dawes County near Chadron later in the evening.
episodes.180430: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed in a moderate CAPE and weak-to-moderate shear environment ahead of an approaching cold front during the afternoon of June 26, 2023. Several reports of wind damage and marginally severe hail were received across central Pennsylvania.
episodes.180431: Upper-level troughing and a weak surface trough to the lee of the Appalachians allowed for the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon of June 27, 2023. A few of these storms were able to produce sporadic wind damage across the Lower Susquehanna Valley.
episodes.180559: A strong cold front coupled with a very unstable atmosphere produced a widespread severe weather outbreak through the late evening hours across Eastern NC. The thunderstorms were mostly wind driven with wind gusts of 65-70 mph,, though one storm produced isolated large hail.
episodes.180581: Some afternoon thunderstorms managed to produce a couple of funnel clouds over parts of northeastern Montana.
episodes.180596: A short wave trough moved across southern New England overnight, triggering a few severe thunderstorms in a very warm and moist environment.
episodes.180597: A short wave trough moved across southern New England overnight, triggering a few severe thunderstorms in a very warm and moist environment.
episodes.180602: A short wave trough moved across southern New England overnight, triggering a few severe thunderstorms in a very warm and moist environment.
episodes.181005: A cold front interacted with a moist and unstable air mass to result in numerous showers and storms across central North Carolina. A few discrete cells first developed during the evening in the northwest Piedmont, resulting in reports of one to two inch hail there. Once the storms consolidated into a line farther south and east, they transitioned into more of a damaging wind event in the late evening and early overnight hours, with numerous reports of trees and power lines down in parts of the northeast Piedmont, Sandhills, and Coastal Plain. There were also many reports of flash flooding in Cumberland County, including Fayetteville.
episodes.181140: A thunderstorm over portions of Carter County produced a brief funnel cloud.
episodes.181193: A severe thunderstorm tracked southeast from Montana across western Harding County before weakening as it moved eastward. The storm produced hail to quarter size and gusty winds.
episodes.181198: A severe thunderstorm developed northwest of Sundance and tracked east-northeast into South Dakota. The storm produced large hail near golf ball size.
episodes.181202: A thunderstorm became severe as it tracked across portions of southwest South Dakota. Large hail around quarter size was reported across portions of the southern Black Hills and adjacent plains to the east.
episodes.181208: A long-lived severe thunderstorm tracked from Wyoming across portions of the northern Black Hills area and southern Butte County, producing large hail and gusty winds.
episodes.181209: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over the Piedmont and Summerset areas, producing hail to golf ball size.
episodes.181210: A thunderstorm quickly became severe in the Rapid City area and tracked eastward onto the adjacent plains. Hail around quarter size accompanied the storm.
episodes.181212: A long-lived supercell thunderstorm developed over the northern Black Hills and tracked eastward across west central South Dakota, producing large hail and wind gusts over 70 mph. Considerable damage to property was reported north of Rapid City as the storm passed through the area.
episodes.181216: A severe thunderstorm developed southeast of Rapid City and tracked east across portions of west central South Dakota. The storm produced large hail and eventually strong wind gusts as it tracked into south central South Dakota and merged into a line with other storms.
episodes.181313: A surface front was shifting south across Georgia with a surge in moist WSW flow off of the Gulf of Mexico under a passing short wave trough and bulk shear of 20-25 kts. Intrusion of drier air from the NW exacerbated DCAPE values well over 1000 J/kg and supported strong downburst winds in scattered severe storms that developed across NE FL in the evening.
episodes.181333: A generally weak/sub-severe cluster of thunderstorms/small mesoscale convective system (MCS) approached the forecast area towards daybreak on the 27th. While the background severe weather environment was modest, strengthening of the system occurred across east-central Oklahoma, with significant severe wind events noted across Payne County. Into the evening of the 27th, a mature MCS developed across far southwestern Kansas/Oklahoma Panhandle and subsequently moved across portions of northern Oklahoma. A few severe caliber wind gusts were measured across the area through the late evening hours.
episodes.181530: A thunderstorm developed in the lee of the Absarokas and became severe as it approached Highway 120. A picture of ping pong ball size hail at the Gooseberry Creek Rest Area was posted on social media. At the Worland airport, a 63 mph wind gust was reported.
episodes.181559: An unstable airmass with a minor weather disturbance resulted in afternoon showers and thunderstorms, with locally severe weather occurring. Isolated locations also experienced flooding, such as portions of Jefferson County where Milligan Canyon Road was washed out in several locations.
episodes.181636: In the late afternoon of the 27th, a few storm cells began to pop up in eastern Colorado. The cell in Kit Carson county rapidly grew and then collapsed and created a 60 mph wind gust. Another cell in northern Yuma county produced hail up to 1.75 inches just before moving into Nebraska.
episodes.181844: A powerful system moved through the Eastern Shore of Maryland, bringing damaging wind gusts with scattered strong to severe thunderstorms.
episodes.182001: A small thunderstorm with weak rotation produced a land spout that was visible from the air. This was reported from a pilot near Burns, OR.
episodes.182006: On the evening of June 25, moderate to heavy rain occurred with rainfall rates briefly reaching up to 4��� per hour. Numerous storms repeatedly traveled over the same area of Southern Grafton County through midnight before the rain ended shortly after. After a short break in the rain activity from midnight through the morning of June 26, showers and thunderstorms began to redevelop across southern New Hampshire by midday. Rounds of heavy showers and thunderstorms moved through Hillsborough county through the afternoon hours with one storm impacting Manchester around 3 PM where 1.5��� of rain fell in an hour. By early evening another round of heavy rain impacted the Wilton and Temple area with an additional 1 to 2��� of rain in less than an hour. This region received heavy rainfall earlier in the afternoon, with this second round bringing rainfall totals of 3 or more inches to the area. During the evening, another round of heavy rain impacted western Cheshire County from 6 pm through 10 pm. The most impactful flooding occurred in the Bristol Community in Grafton County.
episodes.182024: Thunderstorms moved through south central Kansas during the morning hours on June 27th, 2023.  A severe thunderstorm produced thunderstorm wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph and broken tree branches. Nickel sized hail was reported as well.
episodes.182032: A severe thunderstorm near Peetz produced large hail from nickel to golfball size.
episodes.182086: Very high winds from thunderstorms on 06/27.
episodes.182096: Scattered severe storms developed mostly during peak heating as an upper-level low advanced through the Great Lakes region. Wind shear was weak overall. However instability was sufficient, ranging between 1000 to 1500 J/kg.
episodes.182303: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved into eastern Oklahoma from the northwest during the morning of the 27th. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.182304: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved into northwestern Arkansas from the northwest during the morning of the 27th. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.182424: A few evening thunderstorms turned severe, and produced hail around 1 inch in Walsh county, North Dakota.
episodes.182428: Storms dropped quarter sized hail in Lake of the Woods county in Northern Minnesota and Northeastern North Dakota in the afternoon and evening of June 27th.
episodes.182429: Storms dropped quarter sized hail in Northeastern North Dakota in the afternoon and evening of June 27th.
episodes.182432: An upper level storm system via a powerful jet axis moved around the periphery of High Pressure and drove a cold front into a very unstable atmosphere which provided the lifting mechanism for air parcels which would become severe thunderstorms. The cold front arrived during the heating of the day and plenty of CAPE was present to promote powerful updrafts that would suspend large hailstones. The collapsing of storms created a rush of cooler air (outflow) sending other storms downstream that would produce damaging winds. A couple embedded tornadoes were also noted during this period given the favorable atmosphere across central Arkansas.
episodes.182457: A weak surface trough sagged south of I-64 during the evening hours of June 26th, providing a focus for showers and storms to fire late in the day.  This activity coalesced into a loosely organized line toward sunset. Portions of the line produced winds strong enough to produce isolated wind damage reports in Morgan County before settling further southeast and dissipating overnight.
episodes.182493: Southwest flow aloft, combined with a surface trough, brought several rounds of severe thunderstorms to the area. Hail up to 4 inches in diameter and wind gusts to 63 MPH were reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.182526: Heights lowered aloft as an upper level trough slowly approached the area. Showers and thunderstorms were able to develop along a warm frontal boundary at the surface and an outflow boundary from earlier convection. A cluster of severe thunderstorms was able to produce damaging winds over the waters.
episodes.182548: A stalled frontal boundary just north of southwest New Hampshire allowed for this region of the state to stay in a moist and unstable airmass on the afternoon of June 26th.  Thunderstorms begin to develop during the afternoon hours and continued into the evening.  Most storms remained on the week, except for one isolated storm along the Connecticut River Valley in Cheshire County which became severe.
episodes.182575: On the evening of the 27th, a convective complex developed in the northwestern combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles. This system moved northeast into Texas County in Oklahoma Panhandle where it continued to strengthen and take a more easterly direction into Beaver County. Good dynamics and an unstable airmass lead to cells with in this complex that managed to drop hail between 1 and 4 in diameter and even produced some strong winds. Of which a 114 mph wind gust that was measured by the Beaver mesonet.
episodes.182576: On the evening of the 27th, a convective complex developed in the northwestern combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles. This system moved northeast into Texas County in Oklahoma Panhandle where it continued to strengthen and take a more easterly direction into Beaver County. episodes.182579: An occluded low over Michigan and trough over the East Coast allowed for seasonably strong shear and relatively high mid level lapse rates to overspread the region. This resulted in scattered storms which produced damaging winds and large hail on June 26. Additionally, the cold front stalled in the mountains allowing for scattered storms to continue into the early morning hours of June 27.
episodes.182591: Rounds of scattered thunderstorms resulted in isolated flash flooding in portions of central Virginia on June 26.
episodes.182592: An occluded low over Michigan and trough over the East Coast allowed for seasonably strong shear and relatively high mid level lapse rates to overspread the region. episodes.182594: An occluded low over Michigan and trough over the East Coast allowed for seasonably strong shear and relatively high mid level lapse rates to overspread the region. episodes.182598: Support from an upper low over the Montana and Idaho border as well as increasing surface based instability lead to thunderstorm activity over the east slopes of the Cascades and the Blue Mountains. On the western side of the Blue Mountains just east of the foothills, surface winds, outflows from storms over the mountains, and the area terrain lead to the development of a landspout east of Milton-Freewater.
episodes.182600: An occluded low over Michigan and trough over the East Coast allowed for seasonably strong shear and relatively high mid level lapse rates to overspread the region. This resulted in scattered storms with gusty winds which moved over the Chesapeake Bay late on June 26.

episodes.182608: Heat bursts usually occur at night, are associated with decaying thunderstorms, and are marked by gusty, and sometimes damaging, winds, combining a sharp increase in temperature and a sharp decrease in dew point (humidity). This is what happened on the night of the 26th into early morning on the 27th. A mesonet located near Pampa, TX gusted to 73 mph at 0324 CDT with a temperature observation of 69.4 degrees Fahrenheit, and a dewpoint of 58.6. The very next minute the winds gusted to 89 mph with a temperature of 74.9 and a dewpoint of 56. Ten minutes later at 0334CDT the T/Td was 83/52 which equated to a relative humidity of 35 percent. Five minutes prior to the first gust at 0324CDT the relative humidity was 86 percent. Three separate wind gusts OF 60-65 MPH also occurred at the mesonet located 15 mile NNW of Amarillo between 0344CDT and 0429CDT.
episodes.182640: An initial round of storms developed in the morning of June 26 near a warm front. Later in the day as the warm front lifted north and a cold front approached from the west, additional storms developed and moved over the region.
episodes.182643: An initial round of storms developed in the morning of June 26 near a warm front. Later in the day as the warm front lifted north and a cold front approached from the west, additional storms developed and moved over the region.

episodes.182656: Isolated severe thunderstorms developed and quickly intensified over parts of North Central and Northeast Louisiana on the afternoon of June 27th, along the southern flank and associated outflow of an MCV generated upstream by prior convection across Arkansas and Oklahoma. The air mass just downstream of these thunderstorms was extremely unstable and very moist, with upwards of 4000+ J/kg of instability present along and south of a weak frontal boundary. While low-level flow was more modest, mid-level north to northwesterly winds were between to 20-30 knots. This environment was sufficient for isolated severe thunderstorms to develop along the MCV circulation,  leading to a few isolated damaging wind reports across parts of Union Parish and adjacent Ouachita Parish.

A confirmed tornado began approximately 12 miles W of Albin at 6:42 PM MDT. The tornado damaged a single-family residence and destroyed a farm outbuilding. Minimal shingle damage was was visible at the home, with trees and power lines remaining intact on the property. Debris from the home and outbuilding was thrown several hundred yards to the southeast. Hay bales weighing up to 1400 pounds were moved between one quarter and one half mile from their original location. Further southeast along the track of the tornado, 8 wooden power poles were snapped. The damage then became more sporadic along the track as the tornado moved over mainly open fields before dissipating approximately 9 miles WSW of Albin at 6:50 PM MDT.
